questions.question: A vendor bought oranges at 5 for ₹15 and sold them at 3 for ₹5. Find his loss percent.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price Of 5 oranges = Rs. 15

The selling price of 3 oranges = Rs. 5

**Concept Used:**

Loss = C.P - S.P

Loss percent = (loss/C.P) × 100 percent

**Calculation:**

The cost price of 5 oranges = Rs.15

Cost price of 1 orange = 15/5 = Rs. 3

The cost price of 3 oranges = 3×3 = Rs.9

The selling price of 3 oranges = 5

Loss %= (C.P - S.P) × 100 over C.P

Loss % = (9 - 5) × (100/9) %

Loss % = 400/9 % = 44 4over 9 %

**∴ The loss percentage is 44 4over 9** %

questions.question: For the first part of her journey, Sunita traveled at a speed of 450 m/min and, for the rest of the journey, at a speed 1.4 times her initial speed. If Sunita traveled a total distance of 33.3 km in 1 hour, what was the distance that Sunita traveled at a lower speed?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Speed₁ = 450 meter/min

speed₂ = 1.4 × (speed₁)

The total distance traveled in one hour = 33.3 km

**Concept Used:**

Average speed = total distance/total time

**Calculation:**

Speed₁ = 450 m/min = 450 × 3/50 km/h = 27 km/ h

Speed₂ = 1.4 × (speed₁) = 1.4 × 27 = 37.8 km/h

Total distance traveled in 1 hour = 33.3 km

Let the distance travelled at two speeds be x and (33.3 – x) km

⇒ T₁ + T₂ = 1 hour

⇒ x/S₁ + (33.3 – x)/S₂ = 1

⇒ x/27 + (33.3 – x)/27×1.4 = 1

⇒ (33.3 – x)/ 27 × 1.4 = 1 – x/27

⇒ (33.3 – x)/1.4 = 27 – x

⇒ 33.3 – x = 27 × 1.4 – 1.4x

⇒ 0.4x = 27 × 1.4 – 33.3

⇒ x = (37.8 – 33.3)/0.4

⇒ x = 4.5/0.4 = 11.25 km

**∴ The distance traveled by Sunita at a lower speed is 11.25 km.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__**Calculation:

Now,

Ratio of time = 4.5 : 6.3 = 5 : 7

⇒ (5 + 7) = 12 units = 60 min

⇒ 1 unit = 5 min

So 5 units = 25 min

So the distance was covered at a lower speed = 27 × (25/60) 

⇒ 45/4 = 11.25 km

**∴ The correct answer is 11.25 km.**

questions.question: 40 men can complete a piece of work in 18 days. 9 days after they start working together, 5 more men join them. How many days will they now take to complete the remaining work?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Number of men = 40

Number of days taken by 40 men to complete the work = 18 days 

**Concept Used:**

** **1 day's work = M1D1over W1 = M2D2over W2

**Calculation:**

⇒ Let the work be 1 unit.

⇒ 40 men complete the work in 18 days.

⇒ So, Their 1 day's work = (1)/(18)

⇒ Then, Their 9 day's work = (9)/(18)=(1)/(2)

⇒ Remaining work = 1-(1)/(2)=(1)/(2)

⇒ New number of men = 40 + 5 = 45

⇒ M1D1over W1 =M2D2over W2

⇒ 40 × 18over1 =45 × D2 over 1/2

⇒ D₂ = 8 days

**∴ The time taken to complete the remaining work is 8 days.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Calculation:

According to the question:

⇒ 40 × 9 + 45 × n = 40 × 18

⇒ 45 × n = 40 × 9

⇒ n = 8 days

**∴ The correct answer is 8 days.**

⇒ Sum = (400times 100)/(5) = Rs.8000

questions.question: In an examination, the Average marks of 7 children was 20, that of 3 children was 45, that of another 4 children was 15 and that of 2 children was 0. What is the average marks of all the 16 children? (Correct to one decimal place)
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Average marks of 7 Children = 20

Average marks of 3 children = 45

Average marks of 4 children = 15

Average marks of 2 children = 0

**Concept Used:**

Average = Sum of all terms ÷ Number of terms

Sum of n terms = Average × Number of terms

**Calculation:**

Marks obtained by 7 children = 20 × 7 = 140

Marks obtained by 3 children = 45 × 3 = 135

Marks obtained by 4 children = 15 × 4 = 60

Marks obtained by 2 children = 0 × 2 = 0

Total marks obtained by 16 children = 140 + 135 + 60 + 0 = 335

Average marks of 16 children = 335 ÷ 16 = 20.9

**∴ The Average marks of 16 children are 20.9**

questions.question: A washing machine is sold at a discount of 10% on its marked price. A further discount of 5% on the initial selling price is offered if a person makes the payment in cash. If the marked price of the machine is ₹54,000, how much will a customer paying in cash have to pay for purchasing it?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Marked Price of machine = Rs 54,000

Discount on MP = 10%

Discount on making cash payment = 5%

**Concept Used:**

Selling Price = Marked Price × {1 - (d/100)}

**Calculation:**

Applying a discount of 10%,

⇒ Selling Price = 54000 – 10% of 54000

⇒ Selling Price = 54000-(10)/(100)× 54000=54000-5400=48,600 Rs

Applying a discount of 5% on cash payment,

⇒ Selling Price = 48600 – 5% of 48600

⇒ Selling Price = 48600-(5)/(100)× 48600=48600-2430=46,170 Rs

**∴ The customer has to pay the amount of Rs 46,170 in cash for the machine.**

** [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] __Alternate Method__**Calculation:

First discount = 10%; Second discount = 5%

S.P = 54000 × 90% × 95%

S.P = Rs.46,170

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.46,170.**

questions.question: Find the selling price of an article if a shopkeeper allows two successive discounts of 5% each on the marked price of ₹80.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Successive Discounts = 5%

Marked Price of an article = Rs.80

**Concept Used:**

Selling Price = Marked price × {1 - (d/100)}

**Calculation:**

After the first discount of 5%,

Selling Price = 80 – 5% of 80

Selling Price = 80 - (5/100) × 80 = 80 - 4 = 76

After the second discount of 5%,

The Final Selling Price = 76 – 5% of 76

Final Selling Price = 76 - (5/100) × 76 = 76 - 3.8 = Rs.72.20

**∴ The correct answer is Rs.72.20.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**Calculation:

⇒ S.P = Rs.72.2

∴ The correct answer is Rs.72.20.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers is NOT divisible by 15?
questions.solution:
**Concept Used:**

Divisible by 15 = number should be divisible by 3 and 5

Divisible by 3 = sum of the digits should be divisible by 3.

Divisible by 3 = Unit digit should be either 5 or 0.

**Calculation:**

From the options:

⇒ 2595 = 2 + 5 + 9 + 5 = 21

So, 21 is divisible by 3, and the unit digit is 5, so it will be divisible by 5

So, 2595 will be divisible by 15

⇒ 3195 = 3 + 1 + 9 + 5 = 18

So, 18 is divisible by 3 and the unit digit is 5, so it will be divisible by 5

So, 3195 will be divisible by 15

⇒ 3465 = 3 + 4 + 6 + 5 = 18

So, 18 is divisible by 3 and the unit digit is 5, so it will be divisible by 5

So, 3465 will be divisible by 15

⇒ 2995 = 2 + 9 + 9 + 5 = 25

So 25 is not divisible by 3 and the unit digit is 5, so it will be divisible by 5

So 2995 will not be divisible by 15

**∴ The correct answer is 2995.**

questions.question: If the length, breadth and height of a cuboid are 7.5 m, 22 m and 13 m, respectively, then find the volume of the cuboid.

Volume of cuboid = Length × Breadth × Height

**Calculation:**

Volume of cuboid = Length × Breadth × Height

⇒ Volume of Cuboid = 2145 m³

questions.question: What is the average of first 10 multiples of 6?
questions.solution:
**Concept Used:**

Sum of the Arithmetic Series = (n)/(2)[2a+(n-1)d]

Average = Total sum of values ÷ Total number of values

**Calculation:**

First 10 multiples of 6 = 6, 12, 18, ..., 60

We have, First term, (a) = 6; Common Difference (d) = 6

⇒ Average = (frac{n)/(2)[2a+(n-1)d]}{10}

⇒ Average = (frac{10)/(2)[2times 6+(10-1)times 6]}{10}=(5times [12+54])/(10)

⇒ Average = (330)/(10)=33

**∴ The average of first 10 multiples of 6 is 33.**

questions.question: The price of a bike is ₹75,500. What will be the price of the bike after a reduction of 17%?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Price of bike = Rs 75,500

Reduction Percentage = 17%

**Concept Used:**

Price After Reduction = Original Price – Percentage of Original Price

**Calculation:**

Price after reduction = 75500 – 17% of 17500

Price after reduction = 75500-(17)/(100)times 75500=75500-17×755

Price after reduction = 75500 – 12835 = Rs 62,665.

**∴ The price of a bike after a reduction of 17% is Rs 62,665.**

questions.question: The area of quadrilateral is 336 cm² and the perpendiculars drawn to one diagonal from the opposite vertices are 16 cm and 12 cm long. Find the length of this diagonal.
questions.solution:
**GIVEN:**

Area of quadrilateral = 336 

Perpendiculars to one diagonal from the opposite vertices (CF) = 16 and AE =12 respectively.

**FORMULA USED:**

Area of quadrilateral = 1/2 × diagonal × [sum of perpendiculars on diagonal form opposite vertices].

**CALCULATION:**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c64e06229e71767f9f5ffa49961ede29bcdf37531396df70803999de702f958d.png] 

Area = 1/2 × diagonal × [CF + AE]

⇒ 336 = 1/2 × diagonal × [16 + 12]

⇒ 336 = 1/2 × diagonal × 28 

Diagonal = 336/14 = 24 cm.

**∴ The required length of the diagonal is 24 cm.**
